chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from some of our companions, that he said:
"There is no zakat in raw gold (tibra); rather, it is upon the dinars and dirhams."

key_terms.التِّبْرِ: Raw gold, uncoined or in its natural state

ai.seo_question: What is the zakat ruling for raw gold versus coined gold in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between raw gold (*tibra*) and coined currency (*dinar/dirham*) in Shia jurisprudence, reflecting the view that zakat is primarily a monetary tax on circulating wealth rather than a commodity tax on stored bullion. This ruling underscores the practical application of zakat as a mechanism for liquidity circulation, distinguishing it from the broader concept of *khums* or other forms of wealth purification.
